title: Playbook rehearsal CLI and safe dry-run executor
author: Marisol Gomez
description:
Motivation: On-call responders often need to validate multi-step runbooks before applying changes in production. This PR introduces a lightweight "rehearsal" flow to the incident-bot that executes playbook steps in a dry-run mode against captured synthetic telemetry and read-only control-plane APIs. The goal is to give responders confidence in step ordering, guardrail behaviour, and external integration wiring without performing live mutations.

What this PR adds (high level): 1) playbook-rehearsal CLI: new subcommand 'incident-bot rehearse <playbook-id> --context <snapshot>' that runs steps in dry-run and outputs a step-by-step report with proposed API calls and predicted outcomes; 2) safe dry-run executor: an execution layer that enforces side-effect policies, substitutes mutating calls with simulated responses, and tracks intended state transitions; 3) synthetic traffic harness: a small harness that replays sanitized telemetry events (traces, logs, metrics) from a captured snapshot to validate queries used in runbook conditions; 4) authoring hints: ephemeral checks that lint playbook steps for missing assertions and suggest a sanity-check step where appropriate; 5) telemetry and safety audit: add events that record rehearsal runs to the audit log (no secrets persisted).

Usage notes: The rehearse command accepts either a stored snapshot (snapshot-id) or a live-sanitized capture (--live-snapshot) for short, low-risk rehearsals. Output formats: human, json, and compact-summary. By default the CLI runs with a strict policy that blocks any network calls flagged as "dangerous"; operators can supply an allowlist for approved endpoints via --allowlist (only allowed in admin mode).

Safety and threat model: Rehearsal runs are read-only by default. The executor replaces mutation HTTP calls (POST/PUT/DELETE) with deterministic simulated responses based on simple response templates and historical call traces. Secrets are never sent to the rehearsal harness; we added explicit checks to fail-fast if a playbook references a secret directly. Rehearsals are tracked and visible in the audit timeline so reviewers can see when a playbook was tested and by whom.

Testing and rollout: The feature is behind a feature-flag (rehearsal.cli) gated per-org. Unit and integration tests simulate common runbook patterns (service restart, routing failover, config toggles) against the synthetic harness. We rolled the feature to a small pilot org for two weeks before broad enablement.

Related work: Complements the incident-bot runbook linter and oncall rehearsal ideas in ENG-9071; ties into rollout policies in ENG-9123.

review_comments:
Ethan Chen (2026-02-21): Nice ergonomics for the CLI. Two asks: (1) ensure the simulated responses include realistic rate-limit headers so retry logic is exercised; (2) add a small benchmark for rehearsal runtime on large snapshots.

Marisol Gomez (2026-02-22): Addressed both: added rate-limit header emulation and a microbenchmark test. Also documented expected runtime scaling in rehearsal.md.

Priya Kapoor (2026-02-23): Security note: make explicit that secrets are never included in snapshots — add a canonical sanitizer and an assertion that fails the rehearsal if a secret placeholder is detected.

Marisol Gomez (2026-02-23): Added snapshot sanitizer and explicit assertion; included a CI check to enforce snapshot hygiene.

Jordan Lee (2026-02-24): Left a minor nit on CLI output verbosity flags; approved after Marisol pushed the formatting tweak.

Ethan Chen (2026-02-24): Approved.

Maintainer (automation) (2026-02-25): CI green, merging with squash-merge.

release_notes: Added a CLI-driven playbook rehearsal and dry-run executor that lets responders validate runbooks against sanitized telemetry snapshots before executing live changes. Feature behind feature-flag 'rehearsal.cli' and audited.
notes_for_release: Enablement: org admins must opt in via feature flag and provide allowlist for any approved non-read endpoints. Snapshots must pass the new snapshot-hygiene-check in CI before use in rehearsals.
